Title: Horible public key tricks:
Description:
So, I've always been somewhat annoyed at SSL/TLS.
It requires everyone to go through a complex "ACME" dance just to put up a public website.
Worse, certificates expire every few months, so it's not a one and done thing:
even with automation, maintaining a certificate requires care to ensure the ACME client always has access to DNS records or the web server.

Title: How Much Energy Does Building Distro Packages Use
Description:
Some metrics

When I set up the infrastructure for Casuarina Linux I repurposed an AMD AM4 system with
Ryzen 9 5950X 16-Core CPU (105W TDP) and 32Gb of DDR4 RAM as the build server. I set it up
in our laundry, connected it via a smart plug, and reset its counters. Over the course of the
project I would regularly pull package updates from Chimera Linux, build and install them locally,
and then push them to the repo, which would trigger Buildbot to build and publish them.
